results.title: Purposive sampling: complex or simple? Research case examples
results.content: Novice nurse researchers tend to see purposive sampling as either simple or too difficult ([Tuckett, 2004](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7932468/#bibr34-1744987120927206)) and may therefore default to using a convenience sample for the wrong reasons. Purposive sampling is ‘used to select respondents that are most likely to yield appropriate and useful information’ ([Kelly, 2010](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7932468/#bibr15-1744987120927206): 317) and is a way of identifying and selecting cases that will use limited research resources effectively ([Palinkas et al., 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7932468/#bibr21-1744987120927206)). Previously utilised in healthcare redesign research in the United Kingdom ([Campbell et al., 2004](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7932468/#bibr5-1744987120927206)) as part of a patient journey approach, Matrix sampling is a cost-effective and time-efficient method allowing the stakeholders a level of control over the selected sample. The sample, particularly for qualitative research, is often not analysed by the nursing reader of practice papers ([Gelling et al., 2014](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7932468/#bibr10-1744987120927206)). results.title: What is Purposive Sampling? Methods, Techniques, and ...
results.content: Purposive sampling, also known as judgmental or expert sampling, involves intentional selection of participants based on the researcher’s expertise. The idea behind purposive sampling is to select cases, individuals, or communities that serve as the dataset from which meaningful information pertaining to the research question can be derived. Purposive sampling approaches entail selecting participants based on specified criteria or features related to the research subject. Typical case sampling is a type of purposive sampling in qualitative research used to choose participants who exemplify typical or average instances of the phenomenon being studied. In contrast, purposive sampling focuses specifically on selecting participants with characteristics relevant to the research question. * **What is the purpose of sampling in research?**. Purposive sampling involves intentionally selecting participants based on a purpose, i.e., clear criteria, aligned with research goals, to maximize information richness and gain in-depth insights. Purposive sampling is conducted by defining research objectives, establishing criteria, selecting participants intentionally, recruiting participants, collecting and analyzing data, and drawing conclusions in alignment with the study’s objectives.
